The confidence interval widths grow as the forecast moves further out in time because uncertainty naturally compounds over longer horizons. There are certain risks or events that could push outcomes outside the stated intervals. Extreme volatility driven by unforeseen shocks, such as technological breakthroughs, systemic failures, or natural disasters, could also result in values far above or below the estimated ranges. While these events are harder to quantify, they represent tail risks that fall outside the typical probabilistic bounds anticipated in this forecast.
